Based on the search results, here's information about Mistral Vibe CLI documentation regarding shell commands, allowlist, and permissions:

## Shell Commands Configuration

POSIX bash reads permissions, allowlists, and denylists from [tools.bash]. Native Windows git_bash reads them from [tools.git_bash]; native Windows powershell reads them from [tools.powershell].

## Allowlist and Denylist Setup

You can configure allowed and denied shell commands in your Vibe configuration. An example configuration in ~/.vibe/config.toml shows [tools.bash] with permission = "ask", allowlist = ["ls -la", "cat", "grep -r", "ps aux", "df -h", "du -sh"], and denylist = ["rm", "chmod 777", ":(){ :|:& };:", "wget", "curl.*|sh"]

## Permission Handling

Vibe does not execute arbitrary shell commands without permission. By default, it asks for confirmation before running potentially destructive operations.

## Per-Tool Permissions

Per-tool permissions can also be set in [tools.<tool_name>] blocks. This allows you to configure permissions on a per-tool basis across your Vibe setup.

The documentation shows that Mistral Vibe implements a layered permission system that combines configuration-based allowlists/denylists with interactive approval prompts to maintain control over what shell commands can be executed.

content.content:
# Shell Commands and Allowlists in Vibe Code

According to the documentation, some safe commands are automatically permitted without asking for approval. The page states: "Some safe commands (`ls`, `pwd`, `cat`, `echo`, etc.) are auto-allowed by default."

To extend this allowlist with custom commands, you can modify your `config.toml` file under the bash tool configuration. The documentation provides this example:

```
[tools.bash]
permission = "ask"
allow = ["git status", "pnpm test"]
```

This approach lets you specify additional commands that should execute without prompting. You can add any commands you trust to the `allow` array, while also maintaining a `deny` list to block potentially dangerous operations if needed.

# Configuring Shell Command Permissions in config.toml

Based on the documentation provided, **shell command permissions are not directly configured through allowlists in config.toml**. Instead, the configuration focuses on tool permissions.

## Tool-Based Approach

The documentation describes restricting tool access via:

```toml
enabled_tools = ["serena_*"]
disabled_tools = ["mcp_*", "grep"]
```

These settings use "exact names, glob patterns, and regex with the `re:` prefix."

## Hooks for Shell Commands

For shell command execution, the docs reference **hooks** as the mechanism: "Run arbitrary shell commands before or after tool calls, or after each assistant turn, to gate, audit, or rewrite agent behavior. Declare hooks in a separate `hooks.toml` file."

The documentation indicates that "Per-tool permissions can also be set in `[tools.<tool_name>]` blocks" within the configuration structure, but the specific implementation details for shell command allowlists are not detailed in this excerpt.

**For complete configuration options**, the docs recommend consulting the "Configuration reference" page linked at the end of this section.

content.text:
Based on my search of the official Mistral documentation, here's what I found:

## Shell Commands That Run Without Permission

**Auto-allowed safe commands** include: `ls`, `pwd`, `cat`, `echo`, and other basic safe commands. These are permitted by default without asking for approval.

## How to Add Custom Shell Commands to the Allowlist

You configure this in your `~/.vibe/config.toml` file under the `[tools.bash]` section:

```toml
[tools.bash]
permission = "ask"
allow = ["git status", "pnpm test"]
```

Simply add any commands you trust to the `allow` array. You can also maintain a `deny` list to block potentially dangerous operations:

```toml
[tools.bash]
permission = "ask"
allow = ["ls -la", "cat", "grep -r", "ps aux", "df -h", "du -sh"]
deny = ["rm", "chmod 777", "wget", "curl.*|sh"]
```

The configuration supports:
- **Exact command names** (e.g., `"git status"`)
- **Glob patterns** (e.g., `"git *"`)
- **Regex patterns** (e.g., `"curl.*|sh"`)

## Official Documentation Links

- [Safety, Approvals, and Permissions](https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/safety-approvals-permissions)
- [Configuration Guide](https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/configuration)
- [Mistral Vibe GitHub Repository](https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-vibe)
- [Work with the CLI](https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/work-with-cli)
- [Installation Guide](https://docs.mistral.ai/getting-started/quickstarts/vibe-code/install-cli)

The Security, Approvals, and Permissions page is the most relevant for detailed information about which commands are pre-allowed and how to customize permissions.
